notes.text:
Assume k algebraically closed, trivially valued, characteristic zero, Y smooth integral projective, and actual rational data L_Y=A+D with A ample and D effective. Put sigma=log|s_D|. The exact ample P16.1 grant is used only on Y,A.

The supplied complete BJ4.6 proof claims that positive constant margins make an inequality strict everywhere, then that an exponential difference has a negative limit everywhere. On K=[0,1], g=log x (log0=-infinity) and f_j=log(x+1/j) are extended-valued continuous with f_j decreasing to g. At zero, f_j+epsilon cannot lie under g+epsilon_0 for any finite constants. An outer pair with one exact inner function g and one inner approximating family f_j has no upper triple in that displayed preorder. The exponential limit there is zero. This disproves the displayed directedness argument, not the flattening theorem itself.

There is also an actual geometric counterexample to the divided-net monotonicity inference in the supplied BJ6.21 proof. On Y=P1, take D a point, A=O(1), h_i=(1-i^-2)sigma, L_i=A+(1-i^-2)D, and t_i=1-i^-1 for i>=2. Multiply powers of s_D by a generating system of a clearing power of A: its canonical section maximum is zero, so these are genuine homogeneous section maxima in the actual L_i. They decrease to sigma and satisfy h_i<=t_i sigma. However r_i=h_i-t_i sigma=(i^-1-i^-2)sigma increases at every divisorial valuation with sigma<0. Both the bundle classes and coefficients have the required limits.

A repair for full division with ample remainder is as follows. For homogeneous h<=sigma, BJ6.17 gives decreasing genuine homogeneous section approximants h_i in actual L_i with classes tending to A+D. Compactness of {sigma=-1} permits rational t_i->1 with sup h_i<=-t_i there. Homogeneity gives h_i<=t_i sigma on divisorial points; BJ4.22 extends it everywhere. BJ2.23 literally divides sections to obtain genuine r_i in L_i-t_iD, whose classes tend to A. Choose rational c_i>1 tending to one so c_i A-c1(L_i-t_iD) is ample. Then r_i/c_i is genuine A-psh and normalized to supremum zero. Granted ample compactness supplies a subnet limit r with finite divisorial values h-sigma. Genuine addition and BJ divisorial determination imply h=sigma+r at every point. No decreasing assertion for r_i is made.

For general v<=sigma+C, BJ6.24 gives v=sup_lambda(hat v_lambda+lambda). Scaling removes the domination constant from each homogeneous component. Apply the preceding repair to obtain r_lambda with hat v_lambda=sigma+r_lambda. The family r_lambda+lambda is uniformly upper bounded; ample EP gives its usc supremum r. BJ5.6 preserves divisorial values, and divisorial determination gives v=sigma+r everywhere. Thus the entire reference-dominated genuine cone on Y is sigma+PSH(Y,A), with unique quotient. When D=0 the assertion is immediate. The fixed actual A real-valued continuous section nets from the exact ample grant avoid the separate common-pole flattening issue.

notes.text:
Let k be algebraically closed, trivially valued, characteristic zero and X smooth integral proper of dimension n>=1. Stacks0200/0201 supplies a proper birational quasi-projective refinement of X with integral dense closure. Properness of X makes its immersion into projective space closed. Temkin0904.1592v2 Theorem1.2.1 then supplies a finite projective blowup resolution Y; it is integral smooth projective. Retain pi:Y->X. Stacks0AY8 applies to the normal base with generic fiber Spec k(X), proving pi_*O_Y=O_X and geometrically connected fibers.

Choose a very ample effective H on Y avoiding all finitely many exceptional prime divisors; global generation and the infinitude of k permit this. The effective Weil divisor B=pi_*H is Cartier on the smooth X. Stacks0BFP gives isomorphism at every codimension-one point, so pi^*B=H+E with E effective exceptional. Projection formula identifies original sections, and multiplication by s_E^m embeds H0(Y,mH) in H0(X,mB). Ample growth makes B big. One direct lower bound chooses n independent rational functions, clears their poles by a common section of qH, and obtains binomial(m+n,n) independent monomial sections of mqH. Thus an actual big original bundle exists, without assuming original projectivity.

For ANY retained big rational L, pi_*O and projection formula make pi^*L big. Clear denominators to F on Y. Choose an effective very ample Cartier hyperplane T, without any reducedness or irreducibility assumption. On T a positive ample twist N-F|T is globally generated. A section avoiding its finitely many associated points gives injections F^m|T -> N^m. Stacks0B5T and0BEM give h0(T,N^m)=O(m^(n-1)). Big growth and the restriction exact sequence produce a section of mF-M, where M defines T. Divide its effective divisor and M by m and the clearing denominator: pi^*L=A+D as actual rational bundles, A ample, D effective. All choices are fixed before a target; no finite generation, Bertini, countability or invariance is used.

Let B_pi be the nonisomorphism image. Stacks0BFP(4) says no point above B_pi can be quasi-finite over normal X. Every reduced geometric fiber component there consequently has positive dimension. On such a component F, pi^*L is trivial and O(mD)|F=(-mA)|F is antiample. A nonzero section of an antiample bundle would, by powers, inject sections of a sufficiently large very ample positive power into H0(F,O)=the geometric field, contradicting dimension at least two of that section space. Thus s_D vanishes on the entire geometric fiber; analytic points do not detect fiber nilpotents.

Put P=pi(|D|). It contains B_pi. Above B_pi every fiber is contained in D; outside B_pi fibers are singletons. Hence pi^-1(P)=|D| set-theoretically. Conditional on the standard proper-analytic surjectivity facts, also pi^-1(P^an)=|D|^an and the complements are analytically isomorphic. This saturation, rather than just divisor vanishing on exceptional curves, is what excludes the full polar image in the quotient target condition.

Use the retained geometry and saturated polar image P from n2, and assume the standard compact proper analytic quotient/center facts. For the full reference-dominated original-section cone, the unique genuine quotient Q(u) in PSH(Y,A) is determined by pi^*u-sigma off D and divisorial determination. Its construction and full-cone proof are reconstructed in the paper (using the n1 division repair); the claims in this note concerning that cone are conditional on this identification. Define q_u(x)=max_{pi(y)=x} Q(u)(y), over the entire compact fiber. The maximum is usc because its finite upper-level sets are images of compact upper-level sets. No psh or affine property is asserted on bad fibers. For decreasing quotient nets, nested compact upper-level sets show maxima decrease to the maximum of the limit.

Here is the actual polar test. Choose a nonzero section s of a clearing power mA vanishing on D, by positive-twist generation of its ideal. Put a=m^-1 log|s|<=0, sup a=0 and alpha=1/(n+2). The convex increasing function chi(t)=-(-t)^alpha for t<=-1, extended with slope alpha on [-1,0], has slopes in [0,1]. BJ4.10 gives w=1-(1-a)^alpha as a genuine A-psh function, normalized to zero and -infinity on D. BJ7.47 gives Cap{w<=-t}<=n/((t+1)^(1/alpha)-1). Its sufficient finite-energy integral, with the t^n factor retained, has tail O(t^-2). Thus w is an ACTUAL member of E1(Y,A). Saturation pi^-1(P)=D gives q_{F(w)}=-infinity on all P.

Define E_M(F(psi))=E_raw,A(psi) and, at original mass V=A^n, D_M(mu)=sup_u(E_M(u)-integral q_u dmu), over the actual relative E1 cone. Positive mass on P makes the objective of F(w) infinite. Hence finite dual energy forces mu(P)=0, before lifting a target.

For a continuous map p:S->T between compact Hausdorff spaces, closed C with F=p^-1(C), and a complement homeomorphism j:T\C->S\F, every finite Radon mu with mu(C)=0 has a UNIQUE Radon inverse nu with p_*nu=mu and nu(F)=0. Proof: Lambda(g)=integral_{T\C} g(j(x)) dmu is a positive bounded functional on C(S); Riesz gives Radon nu. Continuous tests give p_*nu=mu. For compact K in T\C, normality gives 0<=g<=1 supported off F and equal to one on p^-1K. Then nu(S\F)>=Lambda(g)>=mu(K). Inner regularity gives zero F mass. On compact K' off F, p^-1(p(K'))=K', so its measure is determined; inner regularity proves uniqueness on the complement and hence globally. Borel and upper-bounded extended integrals then agree by simple functions and monotone convergence. No metrizability, countable exhaustion or selection on C is used.

Apply this with C=P^an and F=D^an. Off these zero-mass sets q_{F(psi)} is the actual psi through the isomorphism. Therefore integral q_u dmu=integral psi dnu and D_M(mu)=E_raw,A^dual(nu). The exact ample grant gives finite D_M iff EVERY genuine relative E1 quotient q_u is integrable. Conversely all-quotient integrability first excludes P via w and then gives the same ample equivalence. This is a proved intrinsic characterization conditional on the stated analytic/cone identification. The absolute singular u is not asserted integrable. The same w, by granted mixed-test integrability, forces all transferred mixed outputs to give P zero mass.
